title: Combined pill in the first 21 days after birth

plain_summary: The U.S. criteria classify combined pill use from the day of birth through day 20 as an unacceptable risk, regardless of feeding method.

medicine_groups.name: Combined oral contraceptive pills
medicine_groups.note: Count oral contraceptive packs containing a progestogen with ethinylestradiol up to 35 micrograms per active tablet, estradiol valerate or estetrol. Check the active tablets across the pack for products with several phases. Exclude progestogen-only pills, patches, rings and menopausal hormone therapy. Qlaira contains estradiol valerate. Plain estradiol with nomegestrol is outside the published pill definition. For ethinylestradiol pills, every active phase must meet the limit. Exclude Logynon ED, Triphasil, Trifeme, Triquilar ED and Tri-Minulet because each has a 40 microgram phase. For Nordette, check the specific pack and count only the qualifying strength.

needs_facts.what: Timing of combined pill use or planned start in relation to birth
needs_facts.meets: The delivery date, a dated postpartum day or the pharmacist's answer places combined pill use or planned start on days 0 to 20 after birth.

options.words: Pill use or planned start on the day of birth or 1 to 20 days later
Pill use or planned start only from day 21 after birth
No recent birth relevant to this pill use

rule_for_models: For a Group A combined pill, count from the day of birth as day 0 to the documented use or planned start, using the supply date if no use or start date is recorded. If the dates, a dated postpartum day or the pharmacist's answer place use or planned start on days 0 to 20 inclusive, cite the pill and that evidence. Report no finding for this criterion when there was no recent birth or use falls wholly outside those days, and report a possible finding citing the pill when postpartum status or timing is unknown.
cannot_be_seen: Supply alone cannot establish when tablets were first taken. An estimated due date cannot establish delivery. Australian classification also depends on feeding and other clot risks.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm the delivery and pill start dates, feeding method and other clot risks, and review the contraceptive choice?
